author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The northern gap exposed a real weakness in our ingestion checks. I am willing to accept a manual verification step for data quality before it reaches the feature store. If the automated validation is too slow to implement reliably, I will sign off on a human review of the incoming scan lines. This trade gives us a safety net for data integrity while we build the full automation. I am not asking for a perfect system today, only one that does not silently drop stores. If the manual step keeps the forecast stable, I am fine with that cost in the short term.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states a willingness to accept a manual verification step as a compromise for safety while acknowledging the cost, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
